Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

charts.title: Net Tangible Assets per Share
charts.annotation: Book equity ÷ share count -- a close proxy for Landsec's own disclosed EPRA NTA/share (£8.82 at FY2026), which adjusts statutory equity for deferred tax and derivatives.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Land Securities Group Plc (Landsec): equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Land Securities Group Plc (Landsec): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Land Securities Group Plc (Landsec): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Land Securities Group Plc (Landsec): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Land Securities Group Plc (Landsec): statutory operating income swings with property revaluations that have nothing to do with letting performance, so Landsec's own reporting leads with EPRA Operating Profit on EPRA Revenue (net rental income and fees, before valuation movements) — FY2026 EPRA Revenue was £860m and EPRA Operating Profit £492m, both ahead of the statutory lines here. Treat this chart as the volatility check, not the headline.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • Gaps between statutory operating income and the EPRA measure in the annual report — the difference is mostly revaluation gains/losses

ntaPerShare.title: Net tangible assets per share
ntaPerShare.content:
NTA (net tangible assets) per share is the standard REIT book-value yardstick: net assets after stripping intangibles, divided by shares in issue. It is the balance-sheet side of a REIT's total return, alongside the dividend.

For Land Securities Group Plc (Landsec): the line here is shareholders' equity ÷ shares outstanding, a close proxy for the company's own disclosed EPRA NTA/share (£13.48 FY2019 falling to £8.59 FY2024 on yield-driven devaluations, then recovering to £8.82 by FY2026). Compare the level against the DCF's intrinsic value per share to see how much of the valuation case is already in the book.

What to watch:

  • NTA/share troughing and inflecting, which marks the bottom of a devaluation cycle
  • Share price relative to NTA/share (the P/NTA discount or premium)
  • Dividends paid per share against NTA erosion — is the payout funded by earnings or by running down book value

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Land Securities Group Plc (Landsec): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Land Securities Group Plc (Landsec): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Land Securities Group Plc (Landsec): the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Land Securities Group Plc (Landsec): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
